sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Du bist dann ein anderer Mensch.
sn.e: She said: you are a different person then.

sn.s: Das war der Satz, um den es die ganze Zeit gegangen ist.
sn.e: That was the sentence the whole thing had been about.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Das stimmt nicht.
sn.e: I said: that is not true.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Doch.
sn.e: She said: yes it is.

sn.s: Und sie hatte recht.
sn.e: And she was right.

sn.s: Auf Deutsch bin ich langsam und einfach und ehrlich.
sn.e: In German I am slow and simple and honest.

sn.s: Auf Englisch bin ich schnell und ich weiche aus.
sn.e: In English I am fast and I dodge.

sn.s: Ich kann auf Englisch um alles herumreden.
sn.e: In English I can talk around anything.

sn.s: Auf Deutsch kann ich das nicht.
sn.e: In German I cannot.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Ich kenne den langsamen Menschen.
sn.e: She said: I know the slow person.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Den anderen kenne ich nicht.
sn.e: She said: I do not know the other one.

sn.s: Sie hat gefragt: Welcher bist du?
sn.e: She asked: which one are you?

sn.s: Ich habe keine Antwort gehabt.
sn.e: I had no answer.

sn.s: Ich habe zwanzig Minuten keine Antwort gehabt.
sn.e: For twenty minutes I had no answer.

sn.s: In diesen zwanzig Minuten ist es schlimmer geworden.
sn.e: In those twenty minutes it got worse.

sn.s: Ich habe angefangen, ihr etwas vorzuwerfen.
sn.e: I started throwing something back at her.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Du fragst nie, wie es mir geht.
sn.e: I said: you never ask how I am.

sn.s: Draussen lag an dem Abend kein Nebel.
sn.e: There was no fog outside that evening.

sn.s: Das war nicht wahr und es war auch nicht ganz falsch.
sn.e: That was not true and it was also not entirely false.

sn.s: Sie ist zwei Sekunden still gewesen.
sn.e: She was quiet for two seconds.

sn.s: Dann hat sie gesagt: Das ist ein anderes Thema.
sn.e: Then she said: that is a different subject.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Wir machen es nachher.
sn.e: She said: we will do it afterwards.

sn.s: Und sie hat es nachher wirklich gemacht.
sn.e: And she really did do it afterwards.

sn.s: Sie hat zwei Themen nacheinander gemacht.
sn.e: She did two subjects one after the other.

sn.s: Das kann fast niemand.
sn.e: Almost nobody can do that.

sn.s: Es war nie laut.
sn.e: It was never loud.

sn.s: Niemand hat geschrien.
sn.e: Nobody shouted.

sn.s: Es war die ganze Zeit sehr genau.
sn.e: It was very precise the whole time.

sn.s: Nach zwei Stunden haben wir beide das Wahre gesagt.
sn.e: After two hours we both said the true thing.

sn.s: Fast gleichzeitig.
sn.e: Almost at the same time.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Ich habe Angst, dass ich hier nie ganz ankomme.
sn.e: I said: I am afraid that I will never fully arrive here.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Ich habe Angst, dass du wieder gehst.
sn.e: She said: I am afraid that you will leave again.

sn.s: Zwei Sätze und der ganze Streit war erklärt.
sn.e: Two sentences and the whole argument was explained.

sn.s: Und danach war es schlimmer.
sn.e: And afterwards it was worse.

sn.s: Das habe ich vorher nicht gewusst.
sn.e: I did not know that beforehand.

sn.s: Vor dem wahren Satz hofft man noch.
sn.e: Before the true sentence you can still hope.

sn.s: Nach dem wahren Satz liegt er auf dem Tisch.
sn.e: After the true sentence it is lying on the table.

sn.s: Und niemand kann ihn wegnehmen.
sn.e: And nobody can take it away.

sn.s: Um elf hat sie gesagt: Ich kann nicht mehr.
sn.e: At eleven she said: I cannot do any more.

sn.s: Sie hat nicht gesagt: Geh.
sn.e: She did not say: go.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Ich kann nicht mehr.
sn.e: She said: I cannot do any more.

sn.s: Das ist ein Unterschied und ich habe ihn gehört.
sn.e: That is a difference and I heard it.

sn.s: Ich bin gegangen.
sn.e: I left.

sn.s: An der Tür haben wir beide nichts gesagt.
sn.e: At the door neither of us said anything.

sn.s: Kein Ade und kein bis morgen.
sn.e: No Ade and no see you tomorrow.

sn.s: Draussen war es warm und hell.
sn.e: Outside it was warm and light.

sn.s: Im Juli ist es um elf noch nicht ganz dunkel.
sn.e: In July at eleven it is not quite dark yet.

sn.s: Ich bin eine Stunde gelaufen.
sn.e: I walked for an hour.

sn.s: Ich bin der Reuss entlang gelaufen.
sn.e: I walked along the Reuss.

sn.s: Zweimal hin und zurück, wie im Januar.
sn.e: There and back twice, like in January.

sn.s: Diesmal habe ich es gemerkt.
sn.e: This time I noticed.

sn.s: Zu Hause habe ich neun Nachrichten geschrieben.
sn.e: At home I wrote nine messages.

sn.s: Ich habe keine geschickt.
sn.e: I sent none.

sn.s: Die ersten drei waren wütend.
sn.e: The first three were angry.

sn.s: Die nächsten drei waren zu lang.
sn.e: The next three were too long.

sn.s: Die letzten drei waren nur: Es tut mir leid.
sn.e: The last three were only: I am sorry.

sn.s: Alle neun waren falsch.
sn.e: All nine were wrong.

sn.s: Um zwei Uhr habe ich das Handy weggelegt.
sn.e: At two o'clock I put the phone down.

sn.s: Ich habe nicht geschlafen.
sn.e: I did not sleep.

sn.s: Am Morgen war keine Nachricht da.
sn.e: In the morning there was no message.

lessons.title: Zwei Tage nichts
lessons.desc: Silence, on purpose

sn.s: Am Dienstag ist keine Nachricht gekommen.
sn.e: On Tuesday no message came.

sn.s: Am Mittwoch auch nicht.
sn.e: On Wednesday none either.

sn.s: Zwei Tage sind hier eine ganz normale Zeit.
sn.e: Two days is a completely normal length of time here.

sn.s: Für mich waren es zwei sehr lange Tage.
sn.e: For me they were two very long days.

sn.s: Zu Hause redet man am nächsten Morgen.
sn.e: At home you talk the next morning.

sn.s: Man ruft an und redet zwei Stunden.
sn.e: You call and talk for two hours.

sn.s: Man macht es fertig und dann ist es fertig.
sn.e: You finish it and then it is finished.

sn.s: Hier macht man das nicht.
sn.e: Here people do not do that.

sn.s: Hier lässt man es liegen.
sn.e: Here you leave it lying.

sn.s: Nicht aus Kälte.
sn.e: Not out of coldness.

sn.s: Man denkt, dass der andere auch Zeit braucht.
sn.e: You think that the other person needs time too.

sn.s: Das ist die ganze Idee dahinter.
sn.e: That is the whole idea behind it.

sn.s: Man gibt dem anderen Platz.
sn.e: You give the other person space.

sn.s: Und der andere sitzt zu Hause und denkt: es ist vorbei.
sn.e: And the other person sits at home and thinks: it is over.

sn.s: Beide meinen es gut und beide leiden.
sn.e: Both mean well and both suffer.

sn.s: Ich habe am Dienstag Nuno gefragt.
sn.e: On Tuesday I asked Nuno.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Warte.
sn.e: He said: wait.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Wie lange?
sn.e: I said: how long?

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Bis sie schreibt.
sn.e: He said: until she writes.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Und wenn sie nicht schreibt?
sn.e: I said: and if she does not write?

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Sie schreibt.
sn.e: He said: she will write.

sn.s: Er hat es sehr sicher gesagt.
sn.e: He said it very confidently.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Sie hat gesagt, sie kann nicht mehr.
sn.e: He said: she said she could not do any more.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Sie hat nicht gesagt, es ist fertig.
sn.e: He said: she did not say it was over.

sn.s: Das ist der Unterschied.
sn.e: That is the difference.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Hier sagen die Leute genau, was sie meinen.
sn.e: He said: here people say exactly what they mean.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Auch im Streit.
sn.e: He said: in an argument too.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Besonders im Streit.
sn.e: He said: especially in an argument.

sn.s: Das war das Nützlichste an den zwei Tagen.
sn.e: That was the most useful thing about those two days.

sn.s: Am Mittwoch habe ich acht Nachrichten geschrieben.
sn.e: On Wednesday I wrote eight messages.

sn.s: Es war zwei Tage lang grau.
sn.e: It was grey for two days.

sn.s: Im Haus war Ruhezeit und ich habe nichts gehört.
sn.e: In the building it was quiet hours and I heard nothing.

sn.s: Es tut mir leid war zu wenig für diese zwei Tage.
sn.e: Es tut mir leid was not enough for those two days.

sn.s: Ich habe wieder keine geschickt.
sn.e: Again I sent none.

sn.s: Eine Nachricht in dieser Zeit ist gefährlich.
sn.e: A message at a time like that is dangerous.

sn.s: Sie kommt an einem falschen Moment an.
sn.e: It arrives at the wrong moment.

sn.s: Sie ist zu kurz oder zu lang.
sn.e: It is too short or too long.

sn.s: Und der andere liest einen Ton hinein.
sn.e: And the other person reads a tone into it.

sn.s: Das habe ich beim ersten Streit gelernt.
sn.e: I learned that in the first argument.

sn.s: Kurze kalte Nachrichten sind das Schlimmste.
sn.e: Short cold messages are the worst.

sn.s: Ok. Ja. Verstehe.
sn.e: Ok. Yes. I see.

sn.s: Drei Wörter und der ganze Tag ist kaputt.
sn.e: Three words and the whole day is ruined.

sn.s: Man schreibt sie und meint nichts.
sn.e: You write them and mean nothing.

sn.s: Der andere liest sie und hört alles.
sn.e: The other person reads them and hears everything.

sn.s: Ich habe im Büro nicht gut gearbeitet.
sn.e: I did not work well in the office.

sn.s: Marco hat gefragt: Alles gut?
sn.e: Marco asked: all good?

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Es geht so.
sn.e: I said: it is going all right.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Aha.
sn.e: He said: ah.

sn.s: Er hat nicht weiter gefragt.
sn.e: He did not ask further.

sn.s: Am Nachmittag hat er einen Kaffee gebracht.
sn.e: In the afternoon he brought a coffee.

sn.s: Das ist bei ihm die ganze Sprache dafür.
sn.e: With him that is the whole language for it.

sn.s: Am Mittwochabend habe ich mit Rosmarie geredet.
sn.e: On Wednesday evening I talked to Rosmarie.

sn.s: Sie hat mich im Treppenhaus getroffen.
sn.e: She met me in the stairwell.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Du siehst schlecht aus.
sn.e: She said: you look bad.

sn.s: Sie sagt so etwas direkt.
sn.e: She says something like that directly.

sn.s: Ich habe es ihr erzählt.
sn.e: I told her about it.

sn.s: Sie hat lange nichts gesagt.
sn.e: She said nothing for a long time.

sn.s: Dann hat sie gefragt: Hat sie recht?
sn.e: Then she asked: is she right?

sn.s: Nicht: Was hast du gesagt.
sn.e: Not: what did you say.

sn.s: Nicht: Wer hat angefangen.
sn.e: Not: who started it.

sn.s: Sondern: Hat sie recht.
sn.e: But: is she right.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: In einer Sache schon.
sn.e: I said: in one thing, yes.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Dann sag ihr das.
sn.e: She said: then tell her that.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Nur das eine.
sn.e: She said: only that one thing.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Und nichts anderes dazu.
sn.e: She said: and nothing else with it.

sn.s: Das war ein sehr guter Rat.
sn.e: That was very good advice.

sn.s: Ich habe am Donnerstag um sieben geschrieben.
sn.e: On Thursday at seven I wrote.

sn.s: Ich habe geschrieben: Du hast recht wegen dem Englisch.
sn.e: I wrote: you are right about the English.

sn.s: Mehr nicht.
sn.e: Nothing more.

sn.s: Acht Wörter.
sn.e: Eight words.

sn.s: Sie hat nach zwei Stunden geantwortet.
sn.e: She answered after two hours.

sn.s: Sie hat geschrieben: Danke.
sn.e: She wrote: thank you.

sn.s: Ein Wort.
sn.e: One word.

sn.s: Dann nach einer Minute noch eines.
sn.e: Then after a minute one more.

sn.s: Sie hat geschrieben: Samstag?
sn.e: She wrote: Saturday?

sn.s: Ein Wort und ein Fragezeichen.
sn.e: One word and a question mark.

sn.s: Ich bin am Küchentisch gesessen und habe geheult.
sn.e: I sat at the kitchen table and cried.

sn.s: Wegen einem Wort und einem Fragezeichen.
sn.e: Because of one word and a question mark.

sn.s: Ich habe geschrieben: Ja.
sn.e: I wrote: yes.

sn.s: Zwei Tage und dann vier Wörter zusammen.
sn.e: Two days and then four words between us.

sn.s: Das ist die ganze Kommunikation von dieser Woche.
sn.e: That is the whole communication of that week.

sn.s: Nuno hat gesagt: Siehst du.
sn.e: Nuno said: you see.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Zwei Tage sind zu lang.
sn.e: I said: two days is too long.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Für dich.
sn.e: He said: for you.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Für sie waren es zwei Tage denken.
sn.e: He said: for her it was two days of thinking.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Ihr habt beide gelitten.
sn.e: He said: you both suffered.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Sie hat nur gewusst, dass es aufhört.
sn.e: He said: she just knew that it would stop.

lessons.title: Wieder gut
lessons.desc: Repair, which takes longer than the damage

sn.s: Am Samstag um zwei bin ich zu ihr gegangen.
sn.e: On Saturday at two I went to her place.

sn.s: Ich habe nichts mitgebracht.
sn.e: I brought nothing.

sn.s: Keine Blumen und keine Schokolade.
sn.e: No flowers and no chocolate.

sn.s: Das war richtig.
sn.e: That was right.

sn.s: Blumen nach einem Streit sind hier falsch.
sn.e: Flowers after an argument are wrong here.

sn.s: Sie machen aus einem Gespräch eine Entschuldigung.
sn.e: They turn a conversation into an apology.

sn.s: Und es war kein Gespräch für eine Entschuldigung.
sn.e: And it was not a conversation for an apology.

sn.s: Sie hat die Tür aufgemacht und gesagt: Hoi.
sn.e: She opened the door and said: hi.

sn.s: Nur hoi.
sn.e: Just hi.

sn.s: Wir haben uns nicht umarmt.
sn.e: We did not hug.

sn.s: Wir haben uns an den Tisch gesetzt.
sn.e: We sat down at the table.

sn.s: Sie hatte schon Tee gemacht.
sn.e: She had already made tea.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Ich habe nachgedacht.
sn.e: She said: I have been thinking.

sn.s: Ich habe nachgedacht ist hier der Anfang von einer Versöhnung.
sn.e: Ich habe nachgedacht is the beginning of a reconciliation here.

sn.s: Es heisst: ich habe nicht nur gewartet.
sn.e: It means: I have not only been waiting.

sn.s: Es heisst: ich komme mit etwas.
sn.e: It means: I am coming with something.

sn.s: Sie hat drei Sachen gesagt.
sn.e: She said three things.

sn.s: Die erste war: Ich habe zu wenig gefragt.
sn.e: The first was: I have asked too little.

sn.s: Die zweite war: Ich habe Angst und das ist nicht dein Problem.
sn.e: The second was: I am afraid and that is not your problem.

sn.s: Die dritte war: Und ich mache es trotzdem zu deinem.
sn.e: The third was: and I make it yours anyway.

sn.s: Das war sehr ehrlich und es war schwer für sie.
sn.e: That was very honest and it was hard for her.

sn.s: Ich habe zwei Sachen gesagt.
sn.e: I said two things.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Du hast recht mit dem Englisch.
sn.e: I said: you are right about the English.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Ich weiche aus, wenn es schwierig wird.
sn.e: I said: I dodge when things get difficult.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Nicht nur auf Englisch.
sn.e: I said: not only in English.

sn.s: Das war der wahre Satz und er hat mich zwei Tage gekostet.
sn.e: That was the true sentence and it cost me two days.

sn.s: Wir haben zwei Stunden geredet.
sn.e: We talked for two hours.

sn.s: Danach war es nicht gelöst.
sn.e: Afterwards it was not solved.

sn.s: Es war benannt.
sn.e: It was named.

sn.s: Das ist etwas anderes und es ist genug.
sn.e: That is something else and it is enough.

sn.s: Sie hat eine Kerze angezündet, ohne etwas zu sagen.
sn.e: She lit a candle without saying anything.

sn.s: Am Abend davor war ich bei Timo in der Werkstatt.
sn.e: The evening before I had been at Timo's workshop.

sn.s: Wir sind am Steg gestanden und haben nichts geredet.
sn.e: We stood at the landing stage and said nothing.

sn.s: Um vier hat sie gefragt: Willst du bleiben?
sn.e: At four she asked: do you want to stay?

sn.s: Es tut mir leid ist an diesem Tag nicht gefallen.
sn.e: Es tut mir leid was not said that day.

sn.s: Sie hat gemeint: zum Essen.
sn.e: She meant: for dinner.

sn.s: Sie hat auch das andere gemeint.
sn.e: She also meant the other thing.

sn.s: Ich habe ja gesagt.
sn.e: I said yes.

sn.s: Dann haben wir zusammen gekocht.
sn.e: Then we cooked together.

sn.s: Sie schneidet und ich rühre, wie immer.
sn.e: She cuts and I stir, as always.

sn.s: Wir haben beim Kochen über nichts geredet.
sn.e: While we cooked we talked about nothing.

sn.s: Über den Laden und über das Wetter.
sn.e: About the shop and about the weather.

sn.s: Das war der eigentliche Moment.
sn.e: That was the actual moment.

sn.s: Nicht das Gespräch. Das Kochen danach.
sn.e: Not the conversation. The cooking afterwards.

sn.s: Zwei Menschen machen eine kleine Sache zusammen.
sn.e: Two people do a small thing together.

sn.s: Und dann ist es wieder gut.
sn.e: And then it is fine again.

sn.s: Niemand hat noch einmal Entschuldigung gesagt.
sn.e: Nobody said sorry again.

sn.s: Nicht an dem Abend und nicht später.
sn.e: Not that evening and not later.

sn.s: Das ist hier so und es hat mich zuerst gestört.
sn.e: That is how it is here and at first it bothered me.

sn.s: Ich habe ein Ende gewollt.
sn.e: I wanted an ending.

sn.s: Ich habe einen Satz gewollt: Jetzt ist es wieder gut.
sn.e: I wanted a sentence: now it is fine again.

sn.s: Den Satz sagt hier niemand.
sn.e: Nobody says that sentence here.

sn.s: Es hört einfach auf.
sn.e: It simply stops.

sn.s: Man merkt es am nächsten Morgen.
sn.e: You notice the next morning.

sn.s: Sie hat um sieben Kaffee gemacht für zwei.
sn.e: At seven she made coffee for two.

sn.s: Sie hat meine Tasse genommen.
sn.e: She took my cup.

sn.s: Ich habe eine Tasse in ihrer Küche.
sn.e: I have a cup in her kitchen.

sn.s: Das ist seit April so.
sn.e: That has been the case since April.

sn.s: An diesem Morgen habe ich es zum ersten Mal gesehen.
sn.e: That morning I saw it for the first time.

sn.s: Nuno hat später etwas Gutes gesagt.
sn.e: Nuno said something good later.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Bei uns dauert der Streit drei Stunden.
sn.e: He said: with us the argument lasts three hours.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Und dann ist es fertig und alle umarmen sich.
sn.e: He said: and then it is over and everybody hugs.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Hier dauert der Streit zwanzig Minuten.
sn.e: He said: here the argument lasts twenty minutes.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Und dann dauert das Reparieren zwei Wochen.
sn.e: He said: and then the repairing takes two weeks.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Ich weiss nicht, welches besser ist.
sn.e: He said: I do not know which is better.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Ich weiss nur, das hier hält länger.
sn.e: He said: I only know this one lasts longer.

sn.s: Rosmarie hat mich am Sonntag im Treppenhaus gefragt.
sn.e: On Sunday Rosmarie asked me in the stairwell.

sn.s: Sie hat gefragt: Und?
sn.e: She asked: and?

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Wieder gut.
sn.e: I said: fine again.

sn.s: Sie hat genickt.
sn.e: She nodded.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Das erste Mal ist das schwerste.
sn.e: She said: the first time is the hardest.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Beim zehnten Mal weisst du, dass es aufhört.
sn.e: She said: by the tenth time you know that it stops.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Und dann ist es nur noch anstrengend.
sn.e: She said: and then it is only tiring.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Anstrengend ist besser als Angst.
sn.e: She said: tiring is better than fear.

sn.s: Sie hat dreiundvierzig Jahre mit Walter gehabt.
sn.e: She had forty-three years with Walter.

sn.s: Sie weiss, wovon sie redet.
sn.e: She knows what she is talking about.

sn.s: Zwei Wochen später war alles wieder normal.
sn.e: Two weeks later everything was normal again.

sn.s: Nicht gleich wie vorher.
sn.e: Not the same as before.

sn.s: Normal, aber ein Stück weiter.
sn.e: Normal, but a step further on.

sn.s: Ich frage seitdem öfter.
sn.e: Since then I ask more often.

sn.s: Sie fragt seitdem auch öfter.
sn.e: Since then she asks more often too.

sn.s: Wir sind beide schlecht darin.
sn.e: We are both bad at it.

sn.s: Wir machen es trotzdem.
sn.e: We do it anyway.

sn.s: Im Herbst bin ich zwei Wochen nach Hause gefahren.
sn.e: In the autumn I went home for two weeks.

sn.s: Sie hat mich zum Flughafen gebracht.
sn.e: She took me to the airport.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Komm zurück.
sn.e: She said: come back.

sn.s: Sie hat es als Spass gesagt.
sn.e: She said it as a joke.

sn.s: Sie hat es nicht als Spass gemeint.
sn.e: She did not mean it as a joke.

lessons.title: Zusammenziehen
lessons.desc: Two flats, one lease

sn.s: Im September haben wir angefangen zu suchen.
sn.e: In September we started looking.

sn.s: Zusammenziehen heisst: in eine Wohnung zusammen.
sn.e: Zusammenziehen means: into one flat together.

sn.s: Es ist ein Verb mit zwei Teilen.
sn.e: It is a verb with two parts.

sn.s: Wir ziehen im Frühling zusammen.
sn.e: We are moving in together in the spring.

sn.s: Wir sind zusammengezogen.
sn.e: We have moved in together.

sn.s: Das zusammen steht am Ende.
sn.e: The zusammen stands at the end.

sn.s: Der Anfang war ein Gespräch über Geld.
sn.e: The beginning was a conversation about money.

sn.s: Natürlich war es das.
sn.e: Of course it was.

sn.s: Zwei Wohnungen kosten zusammen zweitausendvierhundert.
sn.e: Two flats cost two thousand four hundred together.

sn.s: Eine Wohnung für zwei kostet ungefähr sechzehnhundert.
sn.e: One flat for two costs about sixteen hundred.

sn.s: Das sind achthundert Franken im Monat.
sn.e: That is eight hundred francs a month.

sn.s: Selina hat es auf ein Blatt gerechnet.
sn.e: Selina worked it out on a sheet of paper.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Das ist nicht der Grund.
sn.e: She said: that is not the reason.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Aber es ist ein guter Grund dazu.
sn.e: She said: but it is a good reason on top.

sn.s: Beides ist wahr und beides zählt.
sn.e: Both are true and both count.

sn.s: Eine Wohnung finden ist hier sehr schwer.
sn.e: Finding a flat is very hard here.

sn.s: In Luzern sind fast keine frei.
sn.e: In Luzern almost none are free.

sn.s: Man sagt: ein Prozent.
sn.e: They say: one per cent.

sn.s: Von hundert Wohnungen ist eine frei.
sn.e: Of a hundred flats, one is free.

sn.s: Bei einer guten Wohnung kommen achtzig Leute schauen.
sn.e: For a good flat eighty people come to look.

sn.s: Achtzig Leute an einem Samstagmorgen.
sn.e: Eighty people on a Saturday morning.

sn.s: Sie stehen im Treppenhaus in einer Reihe.
sn.e: They stand in the stairwell in a line.

sn.s: Alle haben die gleiche Mappe unter dem Arm.
sn.e: They all have the same folder under their arm.

sn.s: In der Mappe sind die gleichen sechs Papiere.
sn.e: In the folder are the same six papers.

sn.s: Man braucht einen Auszug vom Betreibungsregister.
sn.e: You need an extract from the debt register.

sn.s: Das ist ein Papier über Schulden.
sn.e: That is a paper about debts.

sn.s: Es sagt, ob man je Rechnungen nicht bezahlt hat.
sn.e: It says whether you have ever failed to pay bills.

sn.s: Man holt es bei der Gemeinde für siebzehn Franken.
sn.e: You get it from the commune for seventeen francs.

sn.s: Man braucht drei Lohnabrechnungen.
sn.e: You need three payslips.

sn.s: Man braucht eine Kopie vom Ausweis.
sn.e: You need a copy of your identity card.

sn.s: In der ersten Wohnung war ein Regal an der Wand.
sn.e: In the first flat there was a shelf on the wall.

sn.s: In der zweiten hing ein Schild von der Vermieterin.
sn.e: In the second there was a sign from the landlady.

sn.s: In der dritten war die Strecke zum Spital zu lang.
sn.e: In the third the route to the hospital was too long.

sn.s: Selina wollte lieber eine alte Wohnung als eine neue.
sn.e: Selina would rather have an old flat than a new one.

sn.s: Der Vertrag ist acht Seiten lang.
sn.e: The contract is eight pages long.

sn.s: Wir gehen jetzt zusammen einkaufen.
sn.e: We go shopping together now.

sn.s: Der Nachbar unten hat eine Werkstatt im Keller.
sn.e: The neighbour downstairs has a workshop in the cellar.

sn.s: Wir ziehen im Sommer um.
sn.e: We are moving in the summer.

sn.s: Im Zimmer hinten hängt eine Lampe von 1970.
sn.e: In the back room hangs a lamp from 1970.

sn.s: Man braucht die Bewilligung.
sn.e: You need the permit.

sn.s: Und man braucht ein Schreiben vom alten Vermieter.
sn.e: And you need a letter from your old landlord.

sn.s: Und dann bekommt man die Wohnung trotzdem nicht.
sn.e: And then you still do not get the flat.

sn.s: Wir haben elf Wohnungen angeschaut.
sn.e: We looked at eleven flats.

sn.s: Wir haben elf Mal alles abgegeben.
sn.e: Eleven times we handed everything in.

sn.s: Wir haben elf Mal nichts gehört.
sn.e: Eleven times we heard nothing.

sn.s: Manchmal kommt eine Absage.
sn.e: Sometimes a rejection comes.

sn.s: Meistens kommt gar nichts.
sn.e: Mostly nothing comes at all.

sn.s: Beim vierten Mal habe ich gefragt, ob es an mir liegt.
sn.e: The fourth time I asked whether it was because of me.

sn.s: An der Bewilligung, am Namen, am Akzent.
sn.e: Because of the permit, the name, the accent.

sn.s: Selina hat gesagt: Vielleicht.
sn.e: Selina said: maybe.

sn.s: Sie hat nicht nein gesagt.
sn.e: She did not say no.

sn.s: Das war ehrlich und es war nicht schön.
sn.e: That was honest and it was not nice.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Beim nächsten Mal schreibe ich allein.
sn.e: She said: next time I will write on my own.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Und dann kommst du mit.
sn.e: She said: and then you come along.

sn.s: Das hat mich zwei Tage geärgert.
sn.e: That annoyed me for two days.

sn.s: Dann habe ich verstanden, dass sie recht hat.
sn.e: Then I understood that she was right.

sn.s: Man nimmt das Werkzeug, das funktioniert.
sn.e: You take the tool that works.

sn.s: Bei der zwölften hat es geklappt.
sn.e: With the twelfth it worked.

sn.s: Klappen heisst: es hat funktioniert.
sn.e: Klappen means: it worked.

sn.s: Es hat geklappt ist ein sehr häufiger Satz.
sn.e: Es hat geklappt is a very common sentence.

sn.s: Die Wohnung ist im zweiten Stock in einem alten Haus.
sn.e: The flat is on the second floor of an old building.

sn.s: Sie hat drei Zimmer und eine Küche mit einem Fenster.
sn.e: It has three rooms and a kitchen with a window.

sn.s: Sie kostet sechzehnhundertfünfzig.
sn.e: It costs one thousand six hundred and fifty.

sn.s: Sie ist zehn Minuten vom Spital.
sn.e: It is ten minutes from the hospital.

sn.s: Sie ist zwanzig Minuten von meinem Bus nach Kriens.
sn.e: It is twenty minutes from my bus to Kriens.

sn.s: Das ist nicht fair und wir haben beide ja gesagt.
sn.e: That is not fair and we both said yes.

sn.s: Die Vermieterin hat uns angerufen.
sn.e: The landlady called us.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Sie haben die Wohnung.
sn.e: She said: you have the flat.

sn.s: Selina hat das Telefon weggelegt und nichts gesagt.
sn.e: Selina put the phone down and said nothing.

sn.s: Dann hat sie gesagt: Also.
sn.e: Then she said: right.

sn.s: Also heisst hier: es ist entschieden.
sn.e: Also here means: it is decided.

sn.s: Danach kommt der ganze Rest.
sn.e: After that comes all the rest.

sn.s: Man kündigt die alte Wohnung.
sn.e: You give notice on the old flat.

sn.s: Man kündigt drei Monate vorher.
sn.e: You give notice three months beforehand.

sn.s: Man kündigt auf einen Termin.
sn.e: You give notice for a fixed date.

sn.s: Es gibt nur vier Termine im Jahr.
sn.e: There are only four dates in the year.

sn.s: Das habe ich zweimal falsch gemacht.
sn.e: I got that wrong twice.

sn.s: Man meldet sich bei der Gemeinde ab und wieder an.
sn.e: You deregister at the commune and register again.

sn.s: Man meldet den Strom und das Internet und die Post.
sn.e: You notify the electricity and the internet and the post office.

sn.s: Man meldet die Krankenkasse und die Bank und die Steuern.
sn.e: You notify the health insurer and the bank and the tax office.

sn.s: Es gibt eine Liste dafür und sie hat vierzehn Punkte.
sn.e: There is a list for it and it has fourteen items.

sn.s: Selina hat sie im Internet gefunden.
sn.e: Selina found it on the internet.

sn.s: Natürlich gibt es eine Liste.
sn.e: Of course there is a list.

sn.s: Am Abend sind wir in der leeren Wohnung gestanden.
sn.e: In the evening we stood in the empty flat.

sn.s: Wir hatten den Schlüssel für zehn Minuten.
sn.e: We had the key for ten minutes.

sn.s: Die Vermieterin hat unten gewartet.
sn.e: The landlady waited downstairs.

sn.s: Drei leere Zimmer und ein Fenster nach Westen.
sn.e: Three empty rooms and a window facing west.

sn.s: Selina ist in der Mitte gestanden.
sn.e: Selina stood in the middle.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Da kommt der Tisch hin.
sn.e: She said: the table goes there.

sn.s: Sie hat auf einen leeren Boden gezeigt.
sn.e: She pointed at an empty floor.

sn.s: Ich habe den Tisch sofort gesehen.
sn.e: I saw the table at once.

lessons.title: Zu Hause anrufen
lessons.desc: Explaining Switzerland to your own family

sn.s: Ich telefoniere jeden Sonntag nach Hause.
sn.e: I phone home every Sunday.

sn.s: Am Anfang war es jeden zweiten Tag.
sn.e: At the start it was every other day.

sn.s: Dann jede Woche.
sn.e: Then every week.

sn.s: Jetzt jeden Sonntag um sechs.
sn.e: Now every Sunday at six.

sn.s: Bei ihnen ist es dann Mittag.
sn.e: For them it is midday then.

sn.s: Es ist immer laut bei ihnen.
sn.e: It is always loud at their end.

sn.s: Es sind immer vier Leute im Zimmer.
sn.e: There are always four people in the room.

sn.s: Alle reden gleichzeitig.
sn.e: Everybody talks at the same time.

sn.s: Das ist normal und ich habe es vergessen.
sn.e: That is normal and I had forgotten it.

sn.s: Nach einem Jahr hier tönt es sehr laut.
sn.e: After a year here it sounds very loud.

sn.s: Das ist eine komische Sache.
sn.e: That is an odd thing.

sn.s: Meine Mutter fragt jedes Mal das Gleiche.
sn.e: My mother asks the same thing every time.

sn.s: Sie fragt: Isst du genug?
sn.e: She asks: are you eating enough?

sn.s: Sie fragt: Ist es kalt?
sn.e: She asks: is it cold?

sn.s: Und dann fragt sie das andere.
sn.e: And then she asks the other thing.

sn.s: Sie fragt: Und? Wann kommst du zurück?
sn.e: She asks: and? When are you coming back?

sn.s: Sie fragt es seit einem Jahr.
sn.e: She has been asking it for a year.

sn.s: Zuerst hat sie gemeint: zu Besuch.
sn.e: At first she meant: for a visit.

sn.s: Seit einem halben Jahr meint sie etwas anderes.
sn.e: For the last six months she has meant something else.

sn.s: Ich habe im Juli zu lange gebraucht für die Antwort.
sn.e: In July I took too long to answer.

sn.s: Zwei Sekunden zu lang.
sn.e: Two seconds too long.

sn.s: Sie hat es gehört.
sn.e: She heard it.

sn.s: Sie hat nichts gesagt.
sn.e: She said nothing.

sn.s: Sie hat über das Wetter geredet.
sn.e: She talked about the weather.

sn.s: Das ist bei ihr das Zeichen.
sn.e: With her that is the signal.

sn.s: Das Schwierigste ist nicht die Frage.
sn.e: The hardest part is not the question.

sn.s: Das Schwierigste ist das Erklären.
sn.e: The hardest part is the explaining.

sn.s: Ich habe versucht, die Waschküche zu erklären.
sn.e: I tried to explain the laundry room.

sn.s: Ich habe von dem Plan an der Wand erzählt.
sn.e: I told them about the plan on the wall.

sn.s: Von dem Tag in der Woche.
sn.e: About the day of the week.

sn.s: Ich habe von den Kühen im September erzählt.
sn.e: I told them about the cows in September.

sn.s: Mein Bruder hat gefragt, ob es dort immer grau ist.
sn.e: My brother asked whether it is always grey there.

sn.s: Ihr Hund im Hintergrund hat die ganze Zeit gebellt.
sn.e: Their dog in the background barked the whole time.

sn.s: Von dem Klopfen an der Decke.
sn.e: About the knocking on the ceiling.

sn.s: Mein Bruder hat gelacht.
sn.e: My brother laughed.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Das erfindest du.
sn.e: He said: you are making that up.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Nein.
sn.e: I said: no.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Doch. Das ist eine Geschichte.
sn.e: He said: yes you are. That is a story.

sn.s: Ich habe zehn Minuten gebraucht und er hat es nicht geglaubt.
sn.e: I needed ten minutes and he did not believe it.

sn.s: Das ist das Problem an diesem Land.
sn.e: That is the problem with this country.

sn.s: Von aussen tönt alles wie ein Witz.
sn.e: From outside everything sounds like a joke.

sn.s: Der Sack mit der Gebühr.
sn.e: The bag with a fee on it.

sn.s: Die Ruhezeit am Sonntag.
sn.e: The quiet hours on Sunday.

sn.s: Das Gewehr im Schrank.
sn.e: The rifle in the cupboard.

sn.s: Die Kerzen am Baum mit dem Eimer daneben.
sn.e: The candles on the tree with the bucket next to it.

sn.s: Jedes einzelne davon tönt erfunden.
sn.e: Every single one of them sounds invented.

sn.s: Von innen ist es einfach Dienstag.
sn.e: From inside it is simply Tuesday.

sn.s: Ich habe aufgehört, die kleinen Sachen zu erzählen.
sn.e: I have stopped telling them the small things.

sn.s: Das ist ein Verlust und ich weiss es.
sn.e: That is a loss and I know it.

sn.s: Es ist der eigentliche Preis von hier sein.
sn.e: It is the real price of being here.

sn.s: Nicht das Geld und nicht das Wetter.
sn.e: Not the money and not the weather.

sn.s: Sondern: die Hälfte von meinem Leben ist nicht erzählbar.
sn.e: But: half my life cannot be told.

sn.s: Nuno hat gesagt: Das kenne ich.
sn.e: Nuno said: I know that.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Nach fünf Jahren erzählst du nur noch das Wetter.
sn.e: He said: after five years you only tell them about the weather.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Und dann ist es auch nicht mehr wahr.
sn.e: He said: and then that stops being true too.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Sie fragen nach dem Wetter in der Schweiz.
sn.e: He said: they ask about the weather in Switzerland.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Und du sagst: es geht.
sn.e: He said: and you say: it is all right.

sn.s: Er hat gesagt: Und dabei ist Fasnacht.
sn.e: He said: and meanwhile it is Fasnacht.

sn.s: Es gibt eine andere Richtung davon.
sn.e: There is another direction to it.

sn.s: Ich erkläre hier auch mein Land.
sn.e: Here I explain my country too.

sn.s: Marianne fragt viel darüber.
sn.e: Marianne asks a lot about it.

sn.s: Sie fragt genau und ohne Urteil.
sn.e: She asks precisely and without judgement.

sn.s: Kurt fragt einmal im Jahr etwas.
sn.e: Kurt asks something once a year.

sn.s: Und dann ist es genau die richtige Frage.
sn.e: And then it is exactly the right question.

sn.s: Ich rede mit ihnen anders über mein Land.
sn.e: I talk about my country differently with them.

sn.s: Ich sehe es von hier aus.
sn.e: I see it from here.

sn.s: Manches ist besser dort und ich sage es jetzt.
sn.e: Some things are better there and I say so now.

sn.s: Manches ist schlechter und das sage ich auch.
sn.e: Some things are worse and I say that too.

sn.s: Vor einem Jahr habe ich nur verteidigt.
sn.e: A year ago I only defended it.

sn.s: Im Oktober bin ich zwei Wochen hingefahren.
sn.e: In October I went there for two weeks.

sn.s: Es war sehr gut und es war komisch.
sn.e: It was very good and it was strange.

sn.s: Alles war laut und alles war spät.
sn.e: Everything was loud and everything was late.

sn.s: Nichts hat angefangen, wann es sollte.
sn.e: Nothing started when it was supposed to.

sn.s: Ich habe mich zweimal darüber geärgert.
sn.e: Twice I got annoyed about it.

sn.s: Mein Bruder hat gesagt: Du bist Schweizer geworden.
sn.e: My brother said: you have become Swiss.

sn.s: Er hat es als Spass gesagt.
sn.e: He said it as a joke.

sn.s: Ich habe drei Tage darüber nachgedacht.
sn.e: I thought about it for three days.

sn.s: Am letzten Abend hat meine Mutter gefragt.
sn.e: On the last evening my mother asked.

sn.s: Sie hat gefragt: Bleibst du dort?
sn.e: She asked: are you staying there?

sn.s: Die gleichen drei Wörter wie Selina.
sn.e: The same three words as Selina.

sn.s: Die gleichen drei Wörter wie Kurt.
sn.e: The same three words as Kurt.

sn.s: Diesmal habe ich nicht zu lange gebraucht.
sn.e: This time I did not take too long.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Ja.
sn.e: I said: yes.

sn.s: Sie hat lange nichts gesagt.
sn.e: She said nothing for a long time.

sn.s: Dann hat sie gesagt: Gut.
sn.e: Then she said: good.

sn.s: Dann hat sie gefragt, wann sie kommen kann.
sn.e: Then she asked when she could come.

sn.s: Das war die beste Antwort von allen.
sn.e: That was the best answer of all.

lessons.title: Später einmal
lessons.desc: A future, said out loud

sn.s: Man redet hier nicht über die Zukunft.
sn.e: People do not talk about the future here.

sn.s: Man macht Pläne für den zwölften März.
sn.e: They make plans for the twelfth of March.

sn.s: Man macht keine Pläne für in fünf Jahren.
sn.e: They do not make plans for five years' time.

sn.s: Das ist der Unterschied und er ist gross.
sn.e: That is the difference and it is big.

sn.s: Ein Datum in drei Wochen ist normal.
sn.e: A date three weeks away is normal.

sn.s: Ein Satz über in zehn Jahren ist fast unhöflich.
sn.e: A sentence about ten years' time is almost rude.

sn.s: Es tönt nach einer Entscheidung.
sn.e: It sounds like a decision already made.

sn.s: Für den anderen mit.
sn.e: For the other person too.

sn.s: Es gibt trotzdem Formen dafür.
sn.e: There are forms for it anyway.

sn.s: Werden ist die richtige.
sn.e: Werden is the correct one.

sn.s: Ich werde bleiben.
sn.e: I will stay.

sn.s: Wir werden umziehen.
sn.e: We will move.

sn.s: Es wird schwierig.
sn.e: It will be difficult.

sn.s: Werden steht an zweiter Stelle und das Verb geht ans Ende.
sn.e: Werden stands in second place and the verb goes to the end.

sn.s: Man braucht es fast nie für die Zukunft.
sn.e: You hardly ever use it for the future.

sn.s: Man braucht das Präsens mit einer Zeit davor.
sn.e: You use the present with a time in front.

sn.s: Im Frühling ziehen wir um.
sn.e: In the spring we are moving.

sn.s: Nächstes Jahr fahren wir nach Portugal.
sn.e: Next year we are going to Portugal.

sn.s: Beides ist Zukunft und beides tönt sicher.
sn.e: Both are the future and both sound certain.

sn.s: Werden braucht man für etwas anderes.
sn.e: Werden is used for something else.

sn.s: Man braucht es, wenn man nicht sicher ist.
sn.e: You use it when you are not certain.

sn.s: Es wird wohl regnen.
sn.e: It will probably rain.

sn.s: Das wird nicht klappen.
sn.e: That will not work.

sn.s: Dann ist es keine Zukunft. Es ist eine Vermutung.
sn.e: Then it is not a future. It is a guess.

sn.s: Für weit weg gibt es zwei kleine Wörter.
sn.e: For far away there are two small words.

sn.s: Irgendwann heisst: einmal, ohne Datum.
sn.e: Irgendwann means: some day, with no date.

sn.s: Später einmal heisst fast das Gleiche.
sn.e: Später einmal means almost the same.

sn.s: Beide sind sehr vorsichtig.
sn.e: Both are very careful.

sn.s: Beide sagen: ich denke daran und ich verlange nichts.
sn.e: Both say: I am thinking about it and I am asking for nothing.

sn.s: Im November hat Selina einen Satz gesagt.
sn.e: In November Selina said a sentence.

sn.s: Draussen lag Nebel und in der Wohnung war es hell.
sn.e: Outside there was fog and in the flat it was light.

sn.s: Die Sonne kommt hier am Abend ins Zimmer.
sn.e: The sun comes into the room here in the evening.

sn.s: Die alte Lampe steht schon in der Ecke.
sn.e: The old lamp is already in the corner.

sn.s: Der Vertrag ist seit Montag unterschrieben.
sn.e: The contract has been signed since Monday.

sn.s: Wir waren in der neuen Wohnung.
sn.e: We were in the new flat.

sn.s: Wir haben den Boden geputzt.
sn.e: We were cleaning the floor.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: In fünf Jahren machen wir hier eine Wand weg.
sn.e: She said: in five years we will take a wall out here.

sn.s: In fünf Jahren.
sn.e: In five years.

sn.s: Sie hat es beim Putzen gesagt.
sn.e: She said it while cleaning.

sn.s: So kommen hier die grossen Sätze.
sn.e: That is how the big sentences come here.

sn.s: Immer bei etwas anderem.
sn.e: Always in the middle of something else.

sn.s: Immer im Präsens, mit einer Zeit davor.
sn.e: Always in the present, with a time in front.

sn.s: Ich bin mit dem Lappen in der Hand gestanden.
sn.e: I stood there with the cloth in my hand.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: In fünf Jahren.
sn.e: I said: in five years.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Ja. Ungefähr.
sn.e: She said: yes. Roughly.

sn.s: Dann hat sie weiter geputzt.
sn.e: Then she went on cleaning.

sn.s: Ich habe zwei Minuten nichts gesagt.
sn.e: I said nothing for two minutes.

sn.s: Dann habe ich meinen eigenen Satz gesagt.
sn.e: Then I said my own sentence.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Und in zehn Jahren?
sn.e: I said: and in ten years?

sn.s: Sie hat aufgehört zu putzen.
sn.e: She stopped cleaning.

sn.s: Das war das Zeichen.
sn.e: That was the signal.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Was willst du hören?
sn.e: She said: what do you want to hear?

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Nichts Bestimmtes.
sn.e: I said: nothing in particular.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Dann frag nicht.
sn.e: She said: then do not ask.

sn.s: Das war hart und es war auch fair.
sn.e: That was hard and it was also fair.

sn.s: Dann hat sie eine Minute nachgedacht.
sn.e: Then she thought for a minute.

sn.s: Dann hat sie geantwortet.
sn.e: Then she answered.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: In zehn Jahren wohnen wir wahrscheinlich nicht hier.
sn.e: She said: in ten years we probably will not live here.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Wahrscheinlich weiter draussen.
sn.e: She said: probably further out.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Vielleicht mit einem Kind.
sn.e: She said: maybe with a child.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Vielleicht auch nicht.
sn.e: She said: maybe not.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Ich weiss es nicht.
sn.e: She said: I do not know.

sn.s: Und dann hat sie den Satz gesagt.
sn.e: And then she said the sentence.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Aber du bist dabei.
sn.e: She said: but you are in it.

sn.s: Fünf Wörter.
sn.e: Five words.

sn.s: Sie hat es beim Putzen gesagt.
sn.e: She said it while cleaning.

sn.s: Sie hat mich nicht angeschaut.
sn.e: She did not look at me.

sn.s: Ich kenne diesen Ton jetzt.
sn.e: I know that tone now.

sn.s: Vor einem Jahr habe ich ihn nicht gehört.
sn.e: A year ago I did not hear it.

sn.s: Vor einem Jahr habe ich auf ein Gesicht gewartet.
sn.e: A year ago I waited for a face.

sn.s: Jetzt höre ich es an den Wörtern.
sn.e: Now I hear it in the words.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Gut.
sn.e: I said: good.

sn.s: Nur gut.
sn.e: Just good.

sn.s: Sie hat weiter geputzt.
sn.e: She went on cleaning.

sn.s: Nach zwei Minuten hat sie gelacht.
sn.e: After two minutes she laughed.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Du bist jetzt sehr schweizerisch.
sn.e: She said: you have become very Swiss.

sn.s: Ich habe gesagt: Ich habe zwei Jahre gebraucht.
sn.e: I said: it took me two years.

sn.s: Sie hat gesagt: Wir hatten dreissig.
sn.e: She said: we had thirty.

sn.s: Am Abend habe ich alles aufgeschrieben.
sn.e: In the evening I wrote it all down.

sn.s: Das habe ich seit dem ersten Tag gemacht.
sn.e: I have done that since the first day.

sn.s: Am ersten Tag waren es drei Wörter.
sn.e: On the first day it was three words.

sn.s: Grüezi. Gleis. Koffer.
sn.e: Grüezi. Platform. Suitcase.

sn.s: Heute war es ein ganzer Satz.
sn.e: Today it was a whole sentence.

sn.s: Ich habe geschrieben: In zehn Jahren, und ich bin dabei.
sn.e: I wrote: in ten years, and I am in it.

sn.s: Auf Deutsch.
sn.e: In German.

sn.s: Das ist der eigentliche Satz von diesem Jahr.
sn.e: That is the real sentence of that year.

sn.s: Nicht was sie gesagt hat.
sn.e: Not what she said.

sn.s: Sondern in welcher Sprache ich es aufgeschrieben habe.
sn.e: But which language I wrote it down in.

scenarios.title: Grüezi
scenarios.desc: Four people, and not one of them can be passed in silence
scenarios.setting: Your first morning. The lift, the pavement and the bakery, all before eight.

options.feedback: He said mitenand because there are three of you in the lift. You give it straight back, and that is the whole exchange.
Correct and nobody minds. Mitenand would have matched him exactly.
Eight floors of somebody knowing you did not answer. Nobody will mention it.
One word each and you both walk on. That is exactly what it is for.
Warm, and more than a stranger on a pavement was asking for. She will answer you.
Hoi is for people you know. To a stranger it lands as too familiar rather than friendly.
Greeting first, then what you want. That order is not optional here.
She greeted you and you went straight to the order. It is not rude, it is just a bit bare.

options.es: Ich möchte ein Brot und ein Gipfeli und zwei Weggli und Käse.
options.en: I would like a loaf and a Gipfeli and two Weggli and cheese.
options.feedback: No Grüezi at all, and all of it at once. Greet, then order, then add.
You take the leaving word she offered and hand it back. Two syllables and you are out of the door correctly.
Both correct German and both a little German German. Merci and Ade are what you hear in Luzern.
You will hear it, mostly from younger people, and to a woman behind a counter in Luzern it is the wrong register.

scenarios.title: Am Automaten
scenarios.desc: A ticket, a track and eight minutes
scenarios.setting: Zurich airport, underground, with a suitcase and no idea where track seven is.

steps.speaker: Der Automat
steps.en: Where would you like to travel to?

options.feedback: Nach for a town or a country. Short is right, it is a machine.
It works. Nach Luzern is the whole answer.
Zu goes to people and to buildings. Towns and countries take nach.

options.en: Yes, I am finished. Go ahead.
options.feedback: Bitte on its own is the whole of "go ahead". It does a great deal of work in this language.
Honest and fine if you are not. He will wait.
True, possibly, but bare. Einen Moment costs you nothing.

steps.speaker: Eine Frau am Perron
steps.en: Grüezi. Are you looking for something?

options.es: Ja, wo ist Gleis sieben, bitte?
options.en: Yes, where is track seven, please?
options.feedback: Gleis is the numbered track. She will point, or she will walk you there.

options.es: Wo ist der Zug nach Luzern?
options.en: Where is the train to Luzern?
options.feedback: She will understand and answer with a track number, which is what you needed anyway.
Bahnsteig is the German German word. Here it is the Perron, and the number on the board is the Gleis.

steps.speaker: Die Frau am Perron
steps.es: Dort unten, dann rechts. Sie haben noch vier Minuten.
steps.en: Down there, then right. You have four minutes left.

options.feedback: She gave you directions and a warning. Merci vielmal is the right size of thank you for both.
Fine. She did rather more than a plain merci.

options.es: Vier Minuten? Das ist zu wenig!
options.en: Four minutes? That is not enough!
options.feedback: Here four minutes is four minutes. She has told you it is enough by telling you the number.

scenarios.title: Ein Crème, bitte
scenarios.desc: Ordering the coffee, and the word for it
scenarios.setting: The café on the square. Lea is behind the counter and it is not busy.

steps.speaker: Lea
steps.en: Grüezi. What can I get you?

options.feedback: Exactly what you said on your first day, and it works. She will ask you which kind.
The Swiss standard coffee, ordered by its name. This is what you learn on day two.
No greeting and no bitte. She will still bring it and she will still notice.
You did not know the second word and you picked the one you did know. That is the right move every time.
Asking is not a failure. She will tell you, and you will own the word by tomorrow.
She asked which, not whether. You will get whichever she guesses.

steps.speaker: Lea
steps.en: Would you like something to eat as well?

options.feedback: Nein merci is softer than nein on its own, and it is what people actually say.
Coffee and a Gipfeli is the whole Swiss breakfast and nobody will find it odd at three in the afternoon either.
Understood, and a little flat. Merci does the softening.

options.en: (put down four fifty) There you go.
options.feedback: The exact money, so she does not have to give you anything back. Bitte covers the handing over.

options.en: (hand over a twenty) There you go.
options.feedback: Perfectly normal. She will count your change out loud.

options.en: (hand over a two hundred) There you go.
options.feedback: For a four-franc coffee. She will take it, and she will look at you first.

scenarios.title: In der Bäckerei
scenarios.desc: Pointing at things until you have their names
scenarios.setting: Half past six in the morning. Everything is out and nothing is labelled.

options.es: Grüezi. (auf etwas zeigen) Was ist das, bitte?
options.en: Grüezi. (point at something) What is that, please?
options.feedback: Pointing is not cheating. It is how you get the word, and you only need it once per thing.
You know the word already. No article needed with a number.
She will hand it over. A Grüezi in front of it costs one syllable.

steps.speaker: Die Verkäuferin
steps.es: Das ist ein Gipfeli. Möchten Sie eines?
steps.en: That is a Gipfeli. Would you like one?

options.feedback: You take the word she just gave you and use it in the same breath. That is how it sticks.
Also right, and now you have one for the walk and one for later.
She will know exactly what you mean. She has just told you what it is called here, and you used the other word anyway.
She asked an open question and you answered it. This is the point where you add the thing you nearly forgot.
Das ist alles closes the order cleanly.
Fine, if a little short. Nein merci is what she said to you.
Fine, and it costs a few Rappen. Most people here have one in their pocket already.
The answer of somebody who has been here more than a week.
Tüte is the German German word. In Switzerland it is a Sack, and it is not free.

scenarios.title: An der Kasse
scenarios.desc: Paying, and getting a look
scenarios.setting: The Migros till on a Friday. Three people behind you and it moves fast.

steps.speaker: Die Frau an der Kasse
steps.en: Grüezi. Do you have a Cumulus card?

options.feedback: You have no idea what it is and it does not matter. Nein merci is a complete answer.
A fair question with nobody behind you. On a Friday evening she will answer it fast.
She will wait for you to produce it, and you do not have one.

options.en: (hand over thirty francs) There you go.
options.feedback: Five Rappen back and everybody moves on. This is what the .95 is for.
Nobody will sigh at you. They will all watch, though.
Perfectly normal if you did not catch it. She will say the number again, slower.

steps.speaker: Die Frau an der Kasse
steps.es: Fünf Rappen zurück. Möchten Sie den Bon?
steps.en: Five Rappen back. Would you like the receipt?

options.feedback: Two words and you are done. She is already scanning the next person.
Nothing wrong with it at all.
It is nothing, and it is also her till balancing at the end of the day.

steps.speaker: Die Frau an der Kasse
steps.en: Thanks very much. Have a good evening.

options.feedback: Gleichfalls is the one word that gives a good-wish straight back, and it works for every one of them.
Completely fine and what most people say.
She wished you something. Two syllables would have covered it.

scenarios.title: Wo ist die Post?
scenarios.desc: Asking, and understanding half the answer
scenarios.setting: You have been walking in circles for ten minutes and every street looks the same.

options.es: Grüezi. Entschuldigung, wo ist die Post?
options.en: Grüezi. Excuse me, where is the post office?
options.feedback: Greeting, apology, question. Three beats and you have not wasted a second of her time.

options.en: Grüezi. I am looking for the post office.
options.feedback: A statement rather than a question, and it works just as well.
She will help you anyway. One word thrown at a stranger is not how it is done here.

steps.speaker: Die Frau
steps.es: Da vorne links, dann geradeaus, und dann noch einmal rechts.
steps.en: Up ahead on the left, then straight on, and then right again.

options.feedback: Repeating it back is how you find out whether you got it, and it takes two seconds.
Asking again is not embarrassing. Walking twenty minutes the wrong way is.
You did not get it and you have just told her you did. You will be back here in five minutes.

steps.speaker: Die Frau
steps.es: Kommen Sie, ich gehe mit. Es ist nicht weit.
steps.en: Come on, I will come with you. It is not far.

options.es: Merci vielmal. Das ist sehr freundlich.
options.en: Thanks very much. That is very kind.
options.feedback: Accept it. This is the normal answer here and refusing makes it awkward for both of you.
She will let you go. She was not being polite, she genuinely finds it easier than explaining.

options.en: No. I will find it myself.
options.feedback: Flat, and she was doing you a kindness. Nein, nein, das geht schon does the same job without the edge.

steps.speaker: Die Frau
steps.es: So, das gelbe Haus dort. Das ist die Post.
steps.en: There, the yellow building there. That is the post office.

options.feedback: She walked five minutes out of her way. Merci vielmal, not merci.

options.es: Gelb. Das merke ich mir. Merci.
options.en: Yellow. I will remember that. Merci.
options.feedback: And you should. The post office is yellow in every town in the country.
A little thin for somebody who escorted you there.

scenarios.title: Am Brunnen
scenarios.desc: The water is free and somebody will tell you
scenarios.setting: A hot afternoon on the square, with a two-franc bottle of water in your hand.

options.feedback: She is going somewhere with this. Answer and let her get there.

options.es: Grüezi. Ja, es ist warm heute.
options.en: Grüezi. Yes, it is warm today.
options.feedback: The weather, offered back. That is how a conversation starts here.
She greeted you first. One word back leaves the greeting hanging.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Sie müssen das Wasser nicht kaufen. Dort ist ein Brunnen.
steps.en: You do not have to buy water. There is a fountain over there.

options.feedback: The obvious question, and asking it is how you stop buying water for good.
She has just saved you two francs a day. Take it.

options.es: Das Wasser im Brunnen? Nein, merci.
options.en: The water in the fountain? No, thanks.
options.feedback: She is not offering you puddle water. Almost every fountain in the country runs drinking water.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Natürlich. Fast alle Brunnen sind Trinkwasser.
steps.en: Of course. Almost all the fountains are drinking water.

options.feedback: Exactly the right follow-up. There is a sign, and it says kein Trinkwasser.
Go and fill the bottle you already paid for. That is the whole trick.

options.es: In der Stadt? Das ist nicht sauber.
options.en: In town? That is not clean.
options.feedback: It comes off the mountain and it is colder and cleaner than the bottle in your hand.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Das macht jeder am Anfang. Ade.
steps.en: Everybody does that at the start. Goodbye.

options.feedback: She told you something useful and did not make you feel stupid. That deserves the full merci vielmal.
Correct, and it skips the thank you she had earned.

options.en: I am not at the start.
options.feedback: You are, and she was being kind about it.

scenarios.title: Am Samstagabend
scenarios.desc: The shop shut two hours ago
scenarios.setting: Half past six on a Saturday, no milk in the flat, and everything dark.

steps.speaker: Ein Mann vor dem Laden
steps.es: Der ist schon zu. Seit fünf.
steps.en: It has been shut since five.

options.feedback: Say the thing you cannot believe. He will explain it, because everybody here has had this conversation.
Fine, and it ends the conversation before he tells you the useful part.

options.es: Aber es ist erst halb sieben.
options.en: But it is only half past six.
options.feedback: It is, and the shop shut at five regardless. Arguing with the opening hours is a beginner move.

steps.speaker: Der Mann
steps.es: Am Samstag schliessen die Läden früh. Und am Sonntag ist alles zu.
steps.en: On Saturday the shops close early. And on Sunday everything is shut.

options.feedback: Yes. This is the single most useful fact anybody will tell you in your first month.
Sometimes it opens for an hour or two in the morning. That is the whole exception, apart from the station.

options.es: Das ist nicht gut für den Laden.
options.en: That is not good for the shop.
options.feedback: Everybody here has decided otherwise, repeatedly, at the ballot box.

steps.speaker: Der Mann
steps.es: Am Bahnhof ist etwas offen. Auch am Sonntag.
steps.en: There is something open at the station. On Sunday too.

options.en: At the station? Thanks very much!
options.feedback: The station shops are the exception the whole country runs on. Now you know it too.
Yes. And it is open, which on a Sunday is the only thing that matters.
It is a fifteen minute walk and the alternative is no milk until Monday.

steps.speaker: Der Mann
steps.es: Nächstes Mal am Freitag einkaufen. Ade.
steps.en: Do your shopping on Friday next time. Goodbye.

options.en: Thanks. I will do that. Goodbye.
options.feedback: You will, and by the third weekend it will not be a decision any more.
He gave you the rule and the exception in under a minute. Worth the vielmal.
He stopped in the street to save you a wasted Sunday.

scenarios.title: Die Schlüsselübergabe
scenarios.desc: Three keys and a great deal of information
scenarios.setting: Two o’clock, an empty flat, and a landlord who says everything twice.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Grüezi. Also, das ist die Wohnung.
steps.en: Grüezi. So, this is the flat.

options.feedback: His name back to him. Nobody here minds being called by it, and using it says you were listening.
Fine. Merci is the word you will hear back from him.
It is empty because it was handed over cleaned to the corner, which is what he is about to explain.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Der erste Schlüssel ist für die Wohnung, der zweite für das Haus.
steps.en: The first key is for the flat, the second for the building.

options.feedback: There is always a third and it is always the cellar. Asking is quicker than being told twice.
He will say it again anyway. He says everything twice.
You do. The cellar is where your bike is going to live.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Nach dem Duschen müssen Sie das Fenster aufmachen. Sonst gibt es Schimmel.
steps.en: After showering you have to open the window. Otherwise you get mould.

options.feedback: Short and it is a promise. Mould at the handover comes out of your deposit.
Especially in winter. Asking shows you took it as a rule and not as small talk.
He will let that pass and he will remember it.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Die Miete müssen Sie bis am dritten bezahlen. Nicht am vierten.
steps.en: You have to pay the rent by the third. Not the fourth.

options.es: Bis am dritten. Ich schreibe es auf.
options.en: By the third. I will write it down.
options.feedback: He said a date and a not-date. Repeating the date back is the whole answer.
True, and it does not show him you registered which day.
Then a Mahnung comes, it costs twenty francs, and you have just told your landlord you might.

scenarios.title: Am Dienstag gewaschen
scenarios.desc: You used the machine on somebody else’s day
scenarios.setting: The laundry room, two hours later, with your washing still in the machine.

steps.speaker: Frau Steiner
steps.es: Entschuldigung. Der Dienstag ist mein Tag.
steps.en: Excuse me. Tuesday is my day.

options.feedback: She is right, and saying so ends it. Nobody here wants an argument, they want the rota kept.

options.es: Die Maschine ist leer. Ich dachte, es geht.
options.en: The machine was empty. I thought it was fine.
options.feedback: A reason, which she will accept and not agree with. Empty is not the same as free.

options.en: But nobody is using it right now.
options.feedback: That is the argument, and it is the one that makes an enemy in a building you will live in for years.

steps.speaker: Frau Steiner
steps.es: Sie müssen sich in den Plan eintragen. Dann gehört der Tag Ihnen.
steps.en: You have to sign into the rota. Then the day is yours.

options.es: Ich trage mich das nächste Mal ein.
options.en: I will sign myself in next time.
options.feedback: Uses her own verb back. eintragen is the word the whole system runs on.
On the wall by the door. Asking is better than guessing again.
Yes, and it is in the Hausordnung, which she knows and now knows you have not read.

steps.speaker: Frau Steiner
steps.es: Nehmen Sie Ihre Wäsche heraus. Ich brauche die Maschine jetzt.
steps.en: Take your washing out. I need the machine now.

options.feedback: Immediate and one more apology. That closes it properly.
The Tumbler is Tuesday’s too. You are asking for the second half of the day you already took.
Reasonable, and she has been waiting two hours already.

steps.speaker: Frau Amrein
steps.es: Und? War die Frau Steiner böse?

options.feedback: The right answer, and she will report it to the building exactly as you said it.
Honest. She will tell you Frau Steiner is never cross, which is nearly true.

options.en: How do you know about it already?
options.feedback: She always knows already. Asking her that is a joke she will enjoy.

scenarios.title: Beim Hauswart
scenarios.desc: Reporting a problem, in the one hour he is there
scenarios.setting: Five o’clock, the ground floor, and a bathroom light that stopped working yesterday.

options.es: Grüezi. Das Licht im Bad ist kaputt.
options.en: Grüezi. The bathroom light is broken.
options.feedback: Greeting and then the problem in one short sentence. He is waiting for exactly that and nothing else.

options.en: Grüezi. Do you have a moment?
options.feedback: Polite, and it makes him ask what for. He would rather you just said it.
Not unfriendly, just not what this hour is for. He will wait for the actual reason.
Two words. He is already writing it in the book.

options.en: The flat next to Frau Amrein.
options.feedback: He knows exactly which one that is. The number is faster.

options.es: Ich wohne seit einem Monat hier.
options.en: I have been living here a month.
options.feedback: Not the question. He asked which flat.
He will be there at eight. Not five past. Take the time and say thank you.
It could, and you have just made work out of something that was finished.

options.es: Können Sie es heute noch machen?
options.en: Could you still do it today?
options.feedback: You report a problem to him. You do not set his schedule.

options.en: Thanks very much. That was quick.
options.feedback: Four minutes. Noticing it out loud is the closest thing to a compliment he will accept.
Fine. He will nod and pack up.
He will tell you in about six words. It is a fair question.

scenarios.title: Bei der Gemeinde
scenarios.desc: Registering, in eleven minutes
scenarios.setting: Eight in the morning, ticket B twelve, and a folder with four documents in it.

steps.speaker: Der Beamte
steps.es: Grüezi. Was kann ich für Sie tun?
steps.en: Grüezi. What can I do for you?

options.en: Grüezi. I would like to register.
options.feedback: The exact sentence for the exact counter. He will have the form out before you finish it.
True, and he still has to ask what you want. anmelden is the word.

options.en: Grüezi. I need a bank account.
options.feedback: Wrong building. But you do need this first, and the bank will ask for what he is about to give you.
bitte handing something over is one of the four jobs that word does.
It is. Asking costs nothing.
Then this is a second trip. Bring everything, every time.

steps.speaker: Der Beamte
steps.es: Und die Religion? Sie müssen das nicht ausfüllen.
steps.en: And religion? You do not have to fill that in.

options.feedback: Because the church is funded by tax here. He will tell you plainly and it is worth knowing.

options.en: Then I will leave it empty.
options.feedback: He told you it was optional. Taking him at his word is fine.

options.en: Do I have to fill that in?
options.feedback: He has just said you do not. Worth listening to the second half of the sentence.

steps.speaker: Der Beamte
steps.es: So. Das ist die Bestätigung. Willkommen in Luzern.
steps.en: There. That is your confirmation. Welcome to Luzern.

options.feedback: He meant the welcome. It is said without ceremony and it is not nothing.
For the bank and for the insurer. Do not lose it, which is what he is about to say.
It is. Eleven minutes, which will keep surprising you.

scenarios.title: Der Nachbar an der Tür
scenarios.desc: He came up two floors in his socks
scenarios.setting: Three in the afternoon. You have just dragged a table across a wooden floor twice.

steps.speaker: Herr Bucher
steps.es: Grüezi. Ich bin Bucher, von unten.
steps.en: Grüezi. I am Bucher, from downstairs.

options.feedback: You know why he is here and you say so first. That is the whole conversation over in one line.

options.es: Grüezi. Was kann ich für Sie tun?
options.en: Grüezi. What can I do for you?
options.feedback: Polite, and it makes him say the awkward part out loud.

options.es: Grüezi. Es ist erst drei Uhr.
options.en: Grüezi. It is only three o’clock.
options.feedback: It is, and he works at home, which he has not told you yet because you did not let him.

options.en: I did not know that. Sorry.
options.feedback: He is not complaining, he is telling you a fact you needed. Take it that way.

options.en: I will not move anything else.
options.feedback: Concrete, and it is the thing he actually wants.
Yes. And now you know why the building is silent at eleven in the morning.

options.es: Nein. Aber ich kann einen kaufen.
options.en: No. But I can buy one.
options.feedback: That is the answer he came up two floors for, and he did not have to ask for it.
It does, a lot, and asking makes it his suggestion rather than your concession.
He would not have mentioned it otherwise.

options.es: Grüezi, Herr Bucher. Gut, merci. Und Ihnen?
options.en: Grüezi, Herr Bucher. Good, thanks. And you?
options.feedback: Two weeks and a rug later, he is asking. That is not a small thing here — answer it properly and ask back.
Correct and it leaves his question half answered. The Und Ihnen is the other half.
The everyday answer, and it lands as easy rather than formal. He will use it back at you.

scenarios.title: Bei Nuno
scenarios.desc: Friday at seven, and he does come at seven
scenarios.setting: A kitchen after service, a bottle of something, and the first person here who talks fast.

options.feedback: Hoi back, not Grüezi. He offered du and the informal greeting in one word, and taking it is the answer.
Not wrong, and it is a step more formal than what he just gave you. He will not mind and he will notice.
The other informal one. Same register, and it is what you would hear around Zurich and the centre.

steps.speaker: Nuno
steps.es: Und? Wie ist der erste Monat?
steps.en: Well? How is the first month?

options.feedback: Two words and he will laugh, because it is exactly right and he remembers it.
Honest, and it opens the conversation he wants to have.
True, and it is the thing every newcomer says first. He has heard it eighteen years running.

steps.speaker: Nuno
steps.es: Lern die Artikel jetzt. Sofort. Nicht später.
steps.en: Learn the articles now. Straight away. Not later.

options.es: Der Tisch, die Wohnung, das Bad.
options.en: Der Tisch, die Wohnung, das Bad.
options.feedback: You did not agree, you demonstrated. That is the only answer he wanted.
They do. And everybody hears it, which is what he is trying to tell you.
This is the one piece of advice he gives everybody, because nobody gave it to him.

steps.speaker: Nuno
steps.es: Die Fehler sind nicht das Problem. Das Schweigen ist das Problem.
steps.en: The mistakes are not the problem. The silence is the problem.

options.feedback: You do. Forty minutes at an airport without saying a word taught you the same thing.

options.es: Zwei Jahre still. Das ist lang.
options.en: Two years silent. That is a long time.
options.feedback: It is, and he said it about himself. Repeating it back shows you heard which part mattered.

options.es: Ich habe keine Angst vor Fehlern.
options.en: I am not afraid of mistakes.
options.feedback: Everybody says that in the first month. He will simply keep talking to you and find out.

scenarios.title: Das Übliche?
scenarios.desc: Somebody starts your coffee before you get there
scenarios.setting: Quarter past seven, the machine already running, and a question that is not really a question.

options.feedback: Two words, and the second one carries all of it. Gern is how enthusiasm is said here.
You gave her the word back. That is exactly what a regular does with it.
Fair, the first time. But she has watched you order the same thing forty mornings running.
Three words and it is true. She has heard it from everybody who arrives, and she asks anyway.
Correct and closed. One sentence more is what turns this into a conversation.
A closed door. Ja on its own ends it, and she was opening something.
You do. And agreeing with a small direct observation is the whole answer here.

options.en: I do not have much time.
options.feedback: True, and she will point out that the coffee costs the same sitting down.
She has watched you do it for a month. This is a correction and it is meant kindly.
You said it back. Ade is for a guest, bis morgen is for somebody who is coming back.
Not wrong, and it is the more distant of the two. She just gave you the closer one.
You will be there at quarter past seven and both of you know it.

scenarios.title: Vier Minuten
scenarios.desc: The bus is late and somebody looks at the sky
scenarios.setting: A bus stop, rain on the shelter, and a woman with a very old dog.

options.es: Ja. Gestern hat es den ganzen Tag geregnet.
options.en: Yes. Yesterday it rained all day.
options.feedback: Yes plus one sentence. The weather is the door, and you walked through it.
Polite and finished. She will not push, and nothing more will happen.
She knows. She was not making a claim about the weather, she was asking whether you want to talk.
A small failure of your own, offered up. It is the fastest way past the weather.
True and short. She has one too, and she left it on the bus.
Not a mistake. But every no here can carry a second sentence and this one does not.
Seit takes the dative, and this is the answer everybody gives. You will say it a hundred times.
Seit einem. The dative is not optional here and it is the commonest slip in the first year.
Fine. Her next question was going to be how long, so you can save her the trouble.

options.en: I like the town very much.
options.feedback: Gefallen puts the thing in charge: it pleases me. The person goes in the dative and stays there.
Backwards, and it says something else entirely. The town does the pleasing, not you.
Warm enough. Name the thing you like and she will tell you where to sit in spring.

scenarios.title: Woher kommst du?
scenarios.desc: The question you will answer a thousand times
scenarios.setting: An apéro, a glass in your hand, and a man who has asked this before.

options.es: Aus dem Süden. Aus einer kleinen Stadt.
options.en: From the south. From a small town.
options.feedback: The place, then the country. Here the part matters more than the nation, and he will ask which part anyway.
No edge is meant. He asks a man from Bern the same thing and hears it in the vowels.
Charming and it dodges. He will simply ask again, more slowly.

steps.speaker: Marco
steps.es: Und seit wann sind Sie hier?
steps.en: And since when have you been here?

options.feedback: Seit einem Monat, seit einer Woche, seit einem Jahr. Nuno still gets asked after eighteen years.
Understood, and it drops the word that carries the sense. Seit is what makes it a stretch of time.
That is the day you arrived. Seit is the whole month since, and he asked for the month.

options.es: Ich arbeite in einem Büro. Zahlen und Briefe.
options.en: I work in an office. Numbers and letters.
options.feedback: Plain, and plain is the register. Nobody will ask what you earn, and nobody thinks less of the answer.
He asked what you trained as, which here usually means an apprenticeship. Two of three people did one.
Money does not come into this conversation. It will not come into any of them.

steps.speaker: Marco
steps.es: Mein Bruder wohnt auch im Süden.
steps.en: My brother lives in the south too.

options.feedback: You asked back. He has been waiting for somebody to, and now you will hear about the brother.
He opened a door with his own family in it. One question is all it needed.
He gave you something personal. Ja hands it straight back unopened.

scenarios.title: Zum Wohl
scenarios.desc: Eight people, eight glasses, and one rule
scenarios.setting: Half past five, everybody standing, and a plate of olives nobody is eating from.

steps.speaker: Petra
steps.en: Would you like a glass of wine?

options.feedback: Gern does the work, and naming what you want saves a second question.

options.en: No, thank you. A water, please.
options.feedback: Nobody asks twice and nobody minds. A water is a glass, and a glass is all this needs.
She will pour you something. But the offer was a small question with a small answer.
The name, and her eyes, and only then the glass. All three or it does not count.
Half of it. The name is not decoration here, it is the part people notice is missing.
Heard here too, and it is the louder one. Zum Wohl is what an apéro in Luzern mostly says, and it is what she just said.

options.es: Nein. Ich habe gedacht, es gibt Abendessen.
options.en: No. I thought there would be dinner.
options.feedback: Every newcomer makes this mistake once. An apéro is a glass and four olives, and it ends at seven.
Then somebody told you, or you learned it the hard way. Either way you are ahead.
Three olives and four nuts. Not half the plate, which is what hunger does to a newcomer.
It is seven, and at seven everybody puts the glass down at the same moment with no signal at all.
It is early. It is also over, and that is the shape of the thing rather than a judgement on it.
An apéro has an end time the way it has a start time. Asking her to stay puts her in an awkward spot.

scenarios.title: Wollen wir du sagen?
scenarios.desc: A cake, a first name, and a small ceremony
scenarios.setting: Sunday afternoon, your own doorway, and the woman who has said Sie for five weeks.

options.feedback: And then your own first name back. That is the whole ceremony: two first names and a handshake.
You missed it. She gave you her first name after five weeks of not giving it.
You knew the name. She was not telling you the name, she was offering you the du.
The offer comes from the older person and it comes once. Yes is very nearly the only answer.
Still on Sie in the sentence that agrees to leave it. She will laugh, and she will not mind.
Possible, and it is a real refusal of something she thought about for five weeks first.
Dir, not Ihnen. The mouth takes about three weeks to catch up and she has already said so.
The slip everybody makes. She will just say her first name again and wait.
Honest and small, which is the register. Es geht is a real answer here and not a complaint.
Du and the first name in one sentence. That is the pairing, and it is the part that takes practice.
Du and Frau Amrein do not go together. Pick one register and this one is already picked.

options.es: Nein, danke. Ich mache uns einen.
options.en: No, thank you. I will make us one.
options.feedback: Better than accepting. She came across the landing with a cake and you can cross it back.

scenarios.title: Am Tisch
scenarios.desc: Three hours, one small pan, and no hurry at all
scenarios.setting: A flat the same shape as yours, forty years older, and an oven in the middle of the table.

options.feedback: Short is right. This is the first time you have been past her door and neither of you will mention that.
There are two chairs. One of them is hers and has been for forty years.
Setz dich is an instruction shaped like an offer. Raclette is a table you sit at.
Gib mir: the person in the dative, the thing in the accusative. It is the shape of half this evening.

options.en: I am giving you the cheese.
options.feedback: Dir and den. Both cases in one short sentence, and you built it right.
Dir. The person receiving always sits in the dative, with geben, zeigen, schicken and schenken alike.
Fein is for food. Gut is for work and for weather, and using it here marks you out at once.
Understood, and it is the word for a job well done rather than for a plate.
She has made this for you for three hours. Es geht is what you say about a bus.

steps.speaker: Rosmarie
steps.en: Do not drink anything cold with it.

options.en: Then I will have a tea.
options.feedback: Tea or white wine. Whether the rule is true is beside the point: her mother said it.
You will get the explanation, and the explanation is that her mother said so. It is enough.
It may not be. It is also her table, her cheese, and a thing she has believed for seventy years.

scenarios.title: Am Samstag?
scenarios.desc: An invitation with a date in it, and one without
scenarios.setting: After the club, a car park, and somebody deciding how much to commit to.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.en: We should eat together some time.

options.es: Gern. Hast du am Freitag Zeit?
options.en: Gladly. Are you free on Friday?
options.feedback: You turned mal into a date. That is the whole move, and it is the one nobody expects you to make.
Warm and it commits nobody. Mal has no date in it, so nothing will happen unless somebody adds one.
Fair question, and a slightly hard one. Naming a day yourself is easier for both of you.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.es: Freitag geht nicht. Der Dienstag danach?
steps.en: Friday does not work. The Tuesday after?

options.feedback: Settled, and nobody will mention it again until Tuesday. That is what an arrangement is here.
Maybe is not an answer to a date. Say yes or say no and either one is fine.

options.es: Ich schaue noch. Ich sage dir Bescheid.
options.en: I will see. I will let you know.
options.feedback: Honest, and it puts the work on him. He got his calendar out of his bag for this.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.es: Kommst du am Samstag ans Spiel?
steps.en: Are you coming to the match on Saturday?

options.es: Ja, gern. Um wie viel Uhr?
options.feedback: Yes and then the practical question. Both halves, in that order.

options.es: Ich habe leider schon etwas abgemacht.
options.en: Unfortunately I have already arranged something.
options.feedback: Leider, and no reason. Nobody asks what, and the reason stays yours.
It is Wednesday. By local arithmetic three days out is practically the day itself.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.es: Also am Dienstag um halb acht.
steps.en: So Tuesday at half past seven.

options.es: Ich bin um zwanzig nach da.
options.en: I will be there at twenty past.
options.feedback: Five minutes early is on time. Saying so out loud is not fussy here, it is normal.
Done. He will be outside at twenty-five past and so, now, will you.
Half past seven is half past seven. Roughly is what the message four minutes beforehand is for.

scenarios.title: In der Gruppe
scenarios.desc: Fourteen people, eighty messages, and one thumb
scenarios.setting: Your phone on the table at nine in the evening, going off every forty seconds.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.es: Samstag Grillieren bei mir. Wer kommt?
steps.en: Barbecue at my place on Saturday. Who is coming?

options.en: I will be there. At seven?
options.feedback: Short, and it drops the ich. That is the register for messages and a long sentence reads as a problem.

options.es: Ich komme sehr gern und freue mich schon.
options.en: I am coming very gladly and am already looking forward to it.
options.feedback: Nothing is wrong with it. It is four times longer than every other reply and he will ask if you are all right.
A thumb is a yes. Not I have read this: I am coming. People have been counted absent for the difference.
Two words and it is binding. Nobody will ask again, and the bread had better be there.
Now nobody knows whether there is bread. In a group of fourteen, maybe is worse than no.
Fine. Ask in the group rather than to him alone, and somebody will name a thing.
He is seventy-one, he sends the same picture of flowers every morning at six, and nobody answers. Nobody minds either.
Kind, and now there are two messages where the group expected none. He will be pleased.

options.en: It is six in the morning.
options.feedback: It is. He has been up since half past four and this is what he does with the hour.

steps.speaker: Timo
